approachQuestion.prompt:
An archive has n distinct integer labels drawn from 0 through n inclusive. Exactly one label in that range is absent. Return it. The array may be in any order.

Constraints: 0 <= n <= 200000; all labels are distinct and in [0,n].
Example: [3,0,1] -> 2. Edge case: [] -> 0.

Choose the best approach under these constraints.
constraints: Unsigned 32-bit word operations and indexing cost constant time. All labels and indices fit in one word.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

options.text: XOR all integers from 0 through n and all supplied labels into one accumulator. Return it.
options.feedback: Every present label occurs in both collections and cancels; only the absent label occurs once.

options.text: Allocate n+1 Boolean entries, mark supplied labels, and return the unmarked index.
options.feedback: This works for every legal input but retains a range-sized table that cancellation avoids.

options.text: Comparison-sort a copy and scan for the first gap, including missing endpoints.
options.feedback: Sorting handles all gaps correctly, but adds sorting work and a copy.

options.text: Return the XOR of the supplied labels without combining the full range.
options.feedback: For [3,0,1], this returns 2 by coincidence, but [0,1] returns 1 instead of the missing label 2.

feedback.reason: XOR both the complete expected range 0..n and the supplied labels.
details: Initialize one accumulator to zero. XOR each expected label, including n, and each supplied label into it. Labels appearing in both sets cancel, including zero without any special case.

XOR both the complete expected range 0..n and the supplied labels. Every present label cancels twice, leaving the missing one, including a missing zero. Omitting n from the expected scan breaks the domain.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For cancel-expected-and-present, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the array length.
constraints: Unsigned 32-bit word operations and indexing cost constant time. All labels and indices fit in one word.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

feedback.reason: Two linear scans use fixed accumulator and index state.
details: The two scans perform a linear number of fixed-width operations and keep only an accumulator and indices.
Unsigned 32-bit word operations and indexing cost constant time. All labels and indices fit in one word.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The analyzed method does not retain a table or copy.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This is looser than the bounded number of scans.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The input cannot be processed without scanning it in the worst case.
